title: Authorization validators must parse the route's own request proto, since parse_dict silently drops fields it does not define
answers: attach model to gateway endpoint skips model definition permission check
validator reads model_config from wrong request proto so the USE check is skipped
why does an endpoints/models/attach request bypass model definition authorization
shared gateway validator not matching the route request message
body:
Symptom: a user with UPDATE on a gateway endpoint can attach a model definition they have no USE permission on, because the attach body's `model_config` was never checked.
Root cause: the attach route was mapped to mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py:validate_can_update_gateway_endpoint, which parses UpdateGatewayEndpoint, a message with no `model_config` field. `parse_dict` ignores unknown fields, so the nested model definition id was invisible to the validator.
Fix pattern: give each route its own validator that parses that route's request message, as mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py:validate_can_attach_model_to_gateway_endpoint does with AttachModelToGatewayEndpoint. Keep the endpoint UPDATE check and then the USE check on `model_config.model_definition_id`.
Constraints: a shared validator is only safe when the route's proto matches the one it parses. Create and update endpoint routes share mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py:_model_configs_from_request, which is correct only because both messages define `model_configs`. Check the field exists on the message before reusing a validator.
applies: Gateway and other basic-auth validators in mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py that read nested fields from a request body; applies when a route is mapped to a validator written for a different message.
says: Users can attach model definitions to gateway endpoints without having permission to use them.
Attaching a model to an endpoint skips the required model definition permission check.
Prevent unauthorized members from linking restricted models to their own gateway routes.
Endpoint updates should verify that the user has authorization for the referenced model.
Require explicit use permission on model configurations when attaching them to an endpoint.
search: In mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py, authorization validators must parse the route's own request protobuf because parse_dict silently drops undefined fields. Reusing validate_can_update_gateway_endpoint on the attach route parsed UpdateGatewayEndpoint, ignoring model_config and allowing users with endpoint UPDATE to bypass USE checks on model_config.model_definition_id. The route requires validate_can_attach_model_to_gateway_endpoint parsing AttachModelToGatewayEndpoint, while shared validators like _model_configs_from_request are only safe when both request messages define the validated field.
